title.suggested: Allen and Gallagher on the Eve of Their Fight

summary.suggested: The Daily Missouri Democrat reported that Tom Allen and Charley Gallagher would fight the next day on the Mississippi within fifty miles of St. Louis, and listed Allen's next planned matches, starting with McCool on October 10.

metadata.notes: Same page as 349: 'Daily Democrat, Monday Morning, August 16, 1869'.

facts.fact: Allen and Gallagher were to fight between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m. at a point down the Mississippi River within fifty miles of St. Louis, both going on the same boat
Allen said he would just as soon fight as eat bread and molasses
facts.quote: would just as leave fight as eat bread and molasses!

facts.fact: Allen's planned engagements were said to be McCool on October 10 within fifty miles of Cincinnati, then Ned O'Baldwin, Ben Hogan, Joe Goss of England, and Tom Kelley
Tom Kelley had fought Allen's brother in England
Allen and Gallagher were both in the same business (saloon keeping), which the paper said depended partly on the fight's result

notes: The 'engagements' are the paper's forecast, not signed matches. Mentions Allen had a brother who boxed in England. Betting details (Garrison $1000 on Allen) skipped.
